The backend as an SRC node¶

A VisIVO backend that runs next to an SRC node’s data serves it without moving it: the desktop opens a replica in place, and cutouts, moment maps, PV diagrams and source finders run on the node, so only the product leaves it. A discovery catalogue such as SKAVA lists the node’s backend in its DataLink answers and ranks the node on what the backend reports about itself. How the desktop chooses among the nodes is described in SKAVA discovery; starting a backend on a SLURM node in Running the backend on a cluster. The routes below are listed in the Backend API reference.

Settings on a node¶

Variable

Default

Meaning

VISIVO_DATA_ROOTS (or VISIVO_DATA_ROOT)

none

The directories the backend may open (VISIVO_DATA_ROOTS is a :-separated list; VISIVO_DATA_ROOT names one). Every file:// location a client or a catalogue gives it must lie inside them. Without them a single-token backend opens any path; see Sharing one backend between users.

VISIVO_NODE_CODE

none

The node’s code as the catalogue knows it, reported in the status document.

VISIVO_VERSION

the application’s version

What the status document reports as the version.

VISIVO_NODE_STATUS_PUBLIC

1

0 (or false, no) makes /v1/node/status and /v1/metrics require the backend token. /v1/ping stays open.

VISIVO_NODE_GPU

unset

Declares a GPU (1) or none (0) in the status document; unset reports nothing.

VISIVO_CGROUP_ROOT

the process’s own cgroup

The cgroup directory to read limits from (see Node capacity under SLURM).

VISIVO_SOFIA_BIN

sofia2 or sofia on PATH

The SoFiA-2 executable.

VISIVO_FINDER_TIMEOUT_S

3600

The longest a source finder may run, in seconds.

--data-root, --node-code and --version of the SLURM launcher set the first three, and a job given a GPU sets VISIVO_NODE_GPU=1.

Status for whoever routes work to the node¶

Three routes let a catalogue or a monitoring system measure the node without holding a user’s token. They report capacity figures, never users, datasets or paths.

Route

Access

Answer

GET /v1/ping

always open

{"ok": true}: a constant, cheap answer for round-trip probes.

GET /v1/node/status

open unless VISIVO_NODE_STATUS_PUBLIC=0

The status document (JSON).

GET /v1/metrics

open unless VISIVO_NODE_STATUS_PUBLIC=0

The same facts in the Prometheus text format.

The status document:

Field

Content

node_code, version, timestamp, platform

Who answers, which build, when, on which architecture.

cpu

cpus granted (the cgroup quota, never more than the CPUs the process may run on), limited, utilisation_pct since the previous call, pressure_pct (share of the last 10 s with CPU stalls), load_1m (the host’s).

memory

total_bytes (the tightest limit), available_bytes (that limit minus the working set), pressure_pct. Read from cgroup v2, else cgroup v1, with the SLURM grant as one more limit, else the host’s memory: see Node capacity under SLURM.

disk

workspace_free_bytes: free space where products are written.

workers, tasks

The process-pool size; tasks running and queued.

render

Server-side render sessions active and the capacity (VISIVO_RENDER_MAX_SESSIONS).

gpu

As declared by VISIVO_NODE_GPU (true, false or null).

capabilities

kinds (image, cube, dynspec), the available finders, and finder_memory: for each finder, the memory a run needs as factor times the dataset’s bytes plus floor_bytes.

The Prometheus metrics, all gauges (one is left out when its value is unknown): visivo_cpus, visivo_cpu_utilisation_percent, visivo_cpu_pressure_percent, visivo_memory_total_bytes, visivo_memory_available_bytes, visivo_memory_pressure_percent, visivo_workspace_free_bytes, visivo_workers, visivo_tasks_running, visivo_tasks_queued, visivo_render_sessions, visivo_render_capacity, visivo_gpu.

Reporting the status to the catalogue¶

When the catalogue cannot reach the backend (a firewall, a NAT, a tunnel), the backend can send its status document to the catalogue instead, at a fixed interval: a POST to <catalogue>/internal/telemetry/report with the node’s code, the status and the round-trip time measured on the previous report.

Variable

Meaning

VISIVO_SKAVA_TELEMETRY_URL

The catalogue’s base URL (http or https, no credentials in it).

VISIVO_SKAVA_NODE_TOKEN

This node’s telemetry token, issued by the catalogue’s operator.

VISIVO_NODE_CODE

This node’s code in that catalogue.

VISIVO_SKAVA_TELEMETRY_INTERVAL

Seconds between reports (default 10, at least 1).

Reporting is off unless the first three are set; a URL set without the token or the node code, a malformed token or a URL that is not plain http(s) is logged as a warning and nothing is sent. The token travels in the X-Skava-Node-Token header and speaks for this node only. A redirect is treated as a failure and never followed with it. A report that fails is logged once per outage, without the token, and the backend keeps reporting.

How the catalogue registers nodes, issues their tokens and uses the reports is described in the SKAVA documentation: telemetry reports.

SODA on the node¶

The node’s IVOA SODA service cuts and computes on the files under its data roots (backend/app/routers/soda.py). ID is the replica’s file:// URL, as the catalogue’s DataLink hands it out, and must lie inside the data roots. Parameter names are case-insensitive. Requests need the backend token (X-Visivo-Token), except the two VOSI routes.

Route

What it does

GET or POST /soda/sync

A cutout, streamed as FITS. Only OPERATION=CUTOUT (the default) runs synchronously.

/soda/async

A UWS 1.1 job list: POST creates a job (with PHASE=RUN it starts at once) and answers 303 to it; the usual UWS resources follow (phase, results, error, parameters, destruction, …), and DELETE removes a job.

GET /soda/capabilities

VOSI capabilities: the sync and async interfaces. Open.

GET /soda/availability

VOSI availability. Open.

Operations, selected with OPERATION:

OPERATION

Parameters

Result

CUTOUT (default)

POS (CIRCLE, RANGE or POLYGON), or CIRCLE / POLYGON on their own; BAND (metres); TIME

The FITS cutout.

MOMENT (async only)

MOMENT=<order> (0 to 10); optional CHANNELS=<first> <last> (0-based, inclusive) and THRESHOLD=<value> (data below it masked)

The 2-D moment map as FITS.

PV (async only)

PVPATH=<ra1> <dec1> <ra2> <dec2> [...] (ICRS degrees, at least two vertices); optional PVWIDTH=<pixels> (default 1)

The position-velocity diagram as FITS.

RESPONSEFORMAT, when given, must be FITS (application/fits). A parameter an operation does not know is refused rather than ignored. Errors follow DALI: text/plain bodies starting with UsageError: or FatalError:. A valid synchronous cutout that selects nothing answers 204.

A synchronous request with only ID (no POS, CIRCLE, POLYGON, BAND or TIME) returns the file as stored, byte for byte, every HDU and the original header, with its own media type (application/fits for FITS, application/x-hdf5, application/gzip, otherwise application/octet-stream). This is what a DataLink #this link through the service fetches. RESPONSEFORMAT must then be the file’s own format: the node converts nothing.

Products are written in the backend’s workspace, one directory per job, which is removed when the job is aborted, deleted or expires. The UWS result link streams the file; the JSON form of a job (Accept: application/json) also carries output_path, so a client of this backend can open the product in place, as the desktop does.

SKAVA’s catalogue can also answer a SODA request itself by redirecting it (303) to the SODA service of the node that holds the replica; the catalogue side is described in the SKAVA documentation: SODA.

Source finders¶

GET /v1/finders lists the finders the node knows, available or not, with their parameters and, when one is unavailable, why. Two ship with the backend:

  • sofia2: SoFiA-2 for spectral cubes, available when the executable is installed (VISIVO_SOFIA_BIN, or sofia2 / sofia on PATH);

  • photutils: image segmentation for 2-D images, always available.

POST /v1/tasks/sourcefind (dataset_id of a dataset opened on this backend, finder, default sofia2, and params) starts a finder as a task. An unknown finder answers 404, an unavailable one 503, and a dataset of a kind the finder does not handle 422. The finder writes a label mask (FITS on the dataset’s grid) and a catalogue (VOTable) in the workspace under sourcefind/<task_id>/; the task’s result names them, and a cancelled or failed run removes them. A run is stopped after VISIVO_FINDER_TIMEOUT_S seconds.

The available finders and their memory needs are also part of the status document, so a placement service (a Computing Broker) can send a finder job only to a node that has the finder and enough memory for the dataset.
